utterances.text: Oh, yes it does, and I'll tell you now what it has to do with it. You know very well how much help, how much aid was collected and how many people were involved. You could have seen that from the media. The fund enjoyed great support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop here for a second. You had the support of various state organs as well.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's undisputed that you, as a humanitarian fund, were supported from all sides, because it was for the benefit of war victims.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only support I got from the service, you can link that to whoever you want. I don't know whether it was through Frenki, but he was the mediator who helped me get 20 computers for the purpose of retraining the wounded, from the service. At that time, computers were in short supply, and the service supplied them. The entire figure was not higher than 25.000 euros. Believe me, there are pensioned -- pensioners, women, who contributed more to the fund. I don't even know whether it came from the unit, but it was Frenki, at any rate, who brought me those 20 computers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to establish here is that this was an effort that was humane in nature, an effort to support and promote all the combatants who defended the people during combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was also for the purpose of promoting me and giving me a better reputation in your eyes, because it mattered at the time, I think. Well, among the things the unit was responsible for was the liberation of hostages in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that this liberation of the hostages was achieved primarily through political negotiations with the leadership of Republika Srpska, through great media pressure exerted for the hostages to be freed, and I appointed Jovica Stanisic at the time as my special envoy to go there and bring back those hostages, but he was not accompanied by any unit, nor did they free the hostages in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is an objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Frenki appropriated this and took credit for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... question come up here and believe these are just statements by Mr. Milosevic. If there's a question that he believes the witness can answer, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We start with this comment: "It was also for the purpose of promoting me and giving me a better reputation in your eyes, because it mattered at the time." Can you deal with that, Mr. Vasiljkovic? It's suggested it was, I think, for the purposes of promoting the accused. Is there any such notion as that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I believed that mention my foundation in Frenki's speech was -- I'm sorry. I'll speak in Serbian. [Interpretation] Frenki wanted to mention me in that speech in order to reinstate me in a way, because I didn't think I was in their good books, in the good books of the president. And he wanted to promote me, my fund, so that the fund would get more support from the state than it was getting at that period. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the next -- no, wait a moment, Mr. Milosevic. We'll go through this. The next point that's made, among the things the unit was for, I suppose, was support for the liberation of hostages. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know nothing about it except for what I saw on television, and I was shocked to see Jovica Stanisic before the cameras. I always thought of him as chief of the secret service, so I was confused. But I know nothing more about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you know if the unit had anything to do with liberating hostages or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't. I don't know. I don't think so. I never heard such information. But I was in good contacts with individuals, and I think I would learn about it had it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Jovica Stanisic went there with only a couple of people from his own security detail, and he was in touch with his intelligence contacts because he had to find out where all these people were located, he had to gather them in one place and ensure that they are safely transferred to the territory of Yugoslavia. There were no combat operations involved. Their liberation was achieved through political means.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was obvious from the media reporting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally speaking, this speech where he talks about the history of the unit - I don't think this issue relates to me, it relates to all the people who were present there - had I known -- if I had known all that, there would be no need for him to explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness -- you can give evidence in due course, if you want, Mr. Milosevic. It's nothing to do with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One thing that is important to add: Apart from you, there were a lot of important people there. Frenki's objective was to present them in the best possible light and to make an impression. So it was show that was so exaggerated that it couldn't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. possibly have been more pumped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us conclude this. Simatovic's speech was aimed at giving the greatest possible importance to the unit, quoting its history, to raise morale, to create a tradition that, as you described, he tried to create by collecting all sorts of artefacts and data, but as far as I understood you, the speech is loaded with exaggerations and the unit was given credit for things that were actually accomplished by individual members of the unit while they were members of different formations.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Even some members which had nothing to do with the unit, even things that were accomplished by the fund.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw, and it can also be seen on the film, that this centre had just been established there. We see, for example, that the furniture is new, that all of it had just been completed in the sense of organisation, accommodation, et cetera, everything that had to do with the unit. And this is a celebration that was taking place in 1997; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. It was in that period that the unit was the strongest, the strongest I had ever seen it. I mean, that is when it really started looking like a unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice that in these archives, if I can put it this way, that have to do with the conflict in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, that the film about Spegelj was shown and various other clips from other different sources that have nothing to do with the unit itself. That was quite clear, wasn't it? This was a history of the conflict in the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Spegelj is an example of that. What do they have to do with that? Even the state security sector had nothing to do with it. This was done by the military security and Vasiljevic, who testified here before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it clear that in this entire speech and all these explanations, it is not only the unit that is in question but the speech was devoted to a broader subject, the conflict in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, also all the information they have in their archives, including things like the Spegelj film and things like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I defined that very nicely when I said that this was a theatrical thing blown out of proportion and that it was all orchestrated for the president and all the dignitaries who came to pay a visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain this date of the alleged establishment of the unit? Because the unit was not established then. It was only in 1995 or 1996. Is this date then linked to the time when its later individual members started taking part in battle? Can you explain the date? How come this particular date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot link that date to anything. Perhaps I can assume that it was some kind of an internal order at their level to establish some kind of a combat unit of the service. This is just my assumption, because I really cannot link that date to anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That is quite sufficient. And do you remember that Simatovic said on that occasion that the corps of that unit consisted at the time of its establishment of some members of the police of the Republic of Krajina and volunteers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did these individual members of the police and Krajina join the corps of that unit? Only later, after the operations that you talked about. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only after the beginning of August 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this is very important for all those falsehoods that are being presented here, I saw on this film when he says 26 training camps, et cetera. Actually, he is referring to this in the same way in which he refers to the Spegelj film and everything else, because he talks about various kinds of activities that were taking place and that could have nothing to do with that unit or the service itself. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had there been 26 training camps, it would have been a wonderful thing and we could not have had so many victims during the war. And also, the archives would not have been mishandled so badly and unprofessionally. I don't think that this existed. Nothing that I would call a training camp existed. Everybody knows what a training camp consists of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned something in connection with another thing that was blown out of proportion here, and that was a helicopter unit or something, whatever. Do you know that these helicopters he refers to were obtained only in 1993, and I think you yourself confirmed it in your other statement that these were not attack helicopters. They were - how should I put this? - small transport helicopters, two or three of them. That's what they had. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I'm a pilot, I was really interested in this. Two Gazelles, one Bell from the Vietnam war, and later on, a Sikorski was bought, but I think that was bought later. I don't know exactly when it was bought. But this was for important occasions, for show, so I think that's why they bought it. But that is the only helicopter squadron. Believe me, I have a friend in America who has more aircraft than that. And you must admit it sounded impressive. Although you saw all of them there, even the one that was decommissioned, that couldn't work, that did not have a motor, that only had propellers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We saw everything that the unit had there, including the medical equipment and the communications equipment and the combat equipment. Everything was there, lined up at that review; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Captain. Do you remember that at the luncheon that was held after that celebration that I said myself that I was surprised by the level of organisation of the unit and its history and its readiness to combat terrorism? Doesn't it seem to you that this speech of mine was unequivocal proof of the fact that that is when I first learned about this, in 1997?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I refused to attend the luncheon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you weren't at lunch. It was my understanding that you were at the luncheon.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been invited but I refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you refuse to attend?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some political beliefs I had at the time which were opposed to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, it was on my account that you refused to attend the luncheon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then I have a few more questions. During the NATO aggression, were you at Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read about this. The only time that I was in Kosovo and Metohija was in 1992, one single afternoon. That was the only time. Never before that, never after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you're mentioned here too, so I just wanted to establish this.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because according to the information that I have, you were never in Kosovo and Metohija during these operations because, even in 1992, how long were you there? What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had to do with some of the activities pertaining to the fund. And during the NATO aggression, I waged a campaign through the Internet so that the public would be informed about the bombing of my town and my country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong -- I don't know whether this was CNN or perhaps BBC or somebody else. I think it was CNN, though. It was mentioned somewhere that some kind of hacker war was being waged against America from the offices of your fund, and it only had to do with a group of young men who were sending information through the Internet about crimes that the NATO Air Force was committing primarily in the territory of Belgrade, because you did not really have information beyond that, for the entire territory of Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the "heroic" NATO attack against our television and after so many civilians were killed -- of course all of this is under quotation marks. "Heroic," heaven forbid that it be interpreted otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's stick to the evidence rather than comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I feel very strongly about it. I've been talking about war crimes and I just thought that that might be -- I'm sorry. Okay. I respect that, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're being asked about any hacking activities from the office of your fund.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I lived through that. I saw these dead persons, so I feel very strongly about this. Let me have just a bit of water. Well, I decided to establish a network with those few computer-literate persons we had during the sanctions and during those days of poverty and misery and who had just learned to use computers. This was the only way to send the truth out about what was going on in my country and in my town, and this was being inflicted upon them by people who I had considered to be my allies until then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was not hacking. It was only related to --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have to have understanding for them, Mr. Milosevic. They needed a much mightier enemy in order to justify the crimes they committed against us. So then they blew them out of proportion, these young men and the army and whatever. Until the present day, they have not admitted that 21 men took Glina. They say it was the JNA that did it with their forces. Those are Croatian explanations. "What do you mean Captain Dragan this and that?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Would you bear in mind, please, that you're giving evidence, not making speeches. We have enough speeches in this trial. Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Any more questions for this witness? You've got about half an hour left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, you'll be so pleased to hear that I will not use all of that half hour. I just have a few more questions, so it will be less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We talked about officers that you encountered throughout the Republic of Serb Krajina. As far as I can remember, we established that they were all from Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was your knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We established that most of them were volunteers and that a number of them came at the invitation of the authorities of the government of Krajina because that was their native area, and they responded to that call, also voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear of any other version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of anyone who had been ordered to go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite frankly, I have no knowledge to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that if this had to do with active-duty officers of the army of Yugoslavia who hailed from Krajina and who responded to that call, that during that time their status in the army of Yugoslavia was frozen, and they did not have any functions in the army of Yugoslavia when they went as volunteers to Krajina, or, rather, that the army of Yugoslavia had no order issuing authority vis-a-vis them although they, as members of the Yugoslavia army, volunteered to go there? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that from my very own experience, because my best man is an active officer in the army of Yugoslavia. His status was frozen, and he was there for a while and then he returned to service yet again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from a command point of view?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: None whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they continued to receive their salaries because Krajina did not have enough resources to pay their salaries. So this is only material support to the extent to which this went above the budget of the Republic of the Serb Krajina, which was very poor. Even Babic had to admit over here that they would not have survived without our assistance.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that, and I know that that salary came late, because I know that this friend of mine complained that his family had nothing to eat at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at any rate, this was only financial assistance.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I was his superior, and he was an officer of the army of Yugoslavia. So you can imagine how this functioned. So he could not receive any orders from Yugoslavia. He could only receive orders from me, because he volunteered and came to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not receive any orders from the army of Yugoslavia, I assume?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was General Novakovic who was my Supreme Commander then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Novakovic was appointed by the leadership of the Krajina, that is the authorities of the Krajina or, rather, to be more precise, the people's Assembly of the Krajina, to be the commander of the staff of the Serbian army of Krajina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was the highest-ranking officer there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question. In view of the fact that in 1991 and 1993 and 1994 and 1995 all your activity was focused on defence at a time when our people were exposed to enormous crimes and genocide, do you yourself feel proud of what you have done for the defence of your people? Do you feel remorse for anything that you've done?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm absolutely proud of everything I have done. I regret nothing. And if I had it all to do over again, I would do exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this apply to the people you know and that you have personal knowledge of also, the same feeling?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, these are the only kind of people I associated with and worked with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Captain. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Some questions from the amici, Your Honours. Questioned by Mr. Kay:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Vasiljkovic, can we just look at the photographs again that were produced in the exhibit bundle tab 5 of 390.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Uh-huh. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see the third photograph on the first page of tab 5? And you'll remember being asked a question by His Honour Judge Kwon about General Vasiljevic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it would be better if I used this. [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you identified that photograph and possibly another as being examples of General Vasiljevic. If we look to the third page of this section, looking at the photograph at 15:41 where man number 3 has been identified by you as being General Vasiljevic. How certain are you about that identification, or could you be wrong about it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I wasn't close to Vasiljevic. I only saw him a few times. So this is to the best of my knowledge. This is what I thought. But it is possible that I was mistaken. Later on, I did learn that in one place I did make a mistake, but I did the best I could.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I help you, Mr. May? Do you wish me to assist?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a picture of General Dimitrijevic. So the witness was only half wrong, because General Dimitrijevic, at that time, was the head of the administration for security of the army of Yugoslavia, which is what Vasiljevic later became. But this is Dimitrijevic. I assume that the witness made this mistake because he heard that this was the head of security of the army of Yugoslavia, so that may be the reason for the confusion. Because I can see in the picture that this is General Dimitrijevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That clarifies that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It clarifies that. I think you'll probably accept that, won't you, as being more right than your answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps, yes. Perhaps this shows, at any rate, that I was trying to assist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I want to go on to other matters now. You've described your unit as principally being a training unit, but you've also told the Court that you entered into combat operations; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions now about the combat operations, and it concerns the kind of forces that you were against when you were conducting those operations. You've referred to Glina, first of all. How well-armed were the Croats in Glina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were facing a brigade which had armoured vehicles. I mean armoured personnel carriers which had anti-tank weapons that they probably bought somewhere in the West, and they were far better equipped than we were. On our side, we had rudimentary long police weapons. We had a 60-millimetre mortar. That's an infantry-type weapon that you carry along with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move now to another place where you undertook combat operations. Perhaps you could select the next place that you went to, the next combat operation you went on with troops yourself.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Skabrnja, Ljubovo, and Glina. These were the largest ones that I directly commanded and participated in. I mean, of the major operations. And there were about 257 missions deep behind the enemy lines, 40 to 60 metres deep behind the enemy lines. This was destruction of artillery, weapons, the capture of Croatian officers for interrogation and exchange, and collecting intelligence information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Skabrnja, how well-armed were the Croats that you were fighting there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this period, they already had professional brigades. They were equipped with all the technical equipment that they have today. They had good uniforms. It was only then that I got the Croatian uniforms and equipment which I used when working behind the enemy lines in Croatia. But they had modern equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ljubovo. How well-armed were the Croats that you faced there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were armed the way they were in Glina. They had armoured personnel carriers, anti-tank weapons, and 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they better or worse armed than you with your squad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every clash we had with the Croats, they were better armed except when we were working behind their lines, when we had good equipment such as night surveillance equipment, mufflers, GPA equipment, and modern communications systems. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your operations, was there any air fire or air warfare that took place while you were in a combat situation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not command, nor was I able to use air forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your experience, was there any that was used against you by the Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally didn't have this experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all the questions I ask. Re-examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic, when you began your testimony last Wednesday, you told us your reasons for coming. You described your scepticism about the Tribunal and your hope that you could tell the full truth. Your precise words were, "I hope I will be given a chance by the Prosecution, the Trial Chamber, and the accused to convey the full truth." Both myself, Mr. Milosevic, and Mr. Kay now have asked you questions. Do you feel you have had an adequate opportunity to tell the full truth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm grateful for this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I ask you no more questions today and you leave here right now, you are fully satisfied that you have told everything that you have of relevance to the Trial Chamber; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and I think it would not be fair if I didn't say that I am far less sceptical today than I was when I first arrived here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And everything you've said here has been the truth. You're willing to stand behind your words here as being the truth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] To the best of my knowledge. [Interpretation] It was the whole truth, and I am prepared to be held liable for any untruths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a number of questions now to clear up some matters, and I actually have quite a number of questions. I know that you have business plans next Monday. I would ask you, if possible, to keep your answers brief so we do have an opportunity to finish your testimony today. The first question I have for you is regarding the video. You said on Wednesday, and I'll quote from the record, in a question I put to you: "Mr. Vasiljkovic, the video that we have just watched, did it fairly and accurately depict the events as you remember them at the ceremony you attended on that day?" And you said, "Yes, absolutely so." My question to you is the following: It's not a question whether Frenki Simatovic said those things. What you're putting issue in now is whether he really meant those things; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have known Frenki Simatovic for 12 years. I discussed this film with him. I don't think anyone knows him better than I do because we are very close. So everything I have said about Franko Simatovic is true, and I'm sure that he himself will confirm it. We are not talking about a third party but about someone I know very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're not taking issue that the words that we heard on that video, they were the words that came from Frenki Simatovic's mouth. That's not in issue; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your interpretation, or what you've testified here is that this whole ceremony was a piece of fictitious theatre engaged in by you and the other participants there in order to impress an audience. Is that essentially what you're saying about this video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take part in a show. I was in the audience. They were trying to impress me just as they impressed the president and other people they had invited to this show.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're a public figure. Has there ever been another occasion in which you participated or attended another piece of theatre intended to impress an audience, or is this the only occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you speaking of the same unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm speaking at any time. Any time in the former Yugoslavia in connection with this unit or any other public ceremony that you attended with Mr. Milosevic, was there ever another occasion when what was participated in was simply an act of theatre intended to impress an audience?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, two years before this, in Kula, something similar was done, but the guest then was the minister of the police. There were invitees, and of course the unit then was much smaller, less well equipped, but a ceremony was carried out, a speech was read out, and I was given a watch. So this became a sort of tradition concerning that unit. But believe me, I have attended very, very many ceremonies. I receive invitations every day to receptions from the highest-ranking officials and even royalty. So that's something quite normal for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that earlier ceremony, was a fictitious history of the Red Berets read out to the audience?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this document is in existence somewhere, but you will see that this history differs dramatically from the history that was issued in the following year and that the purpose for this was simply to impress the audience, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic has just told us that this unit was established after the war, in 1995. Mr. Frenki Simatovic says it was established on the 4th of May, 1991. One of them is not correct. Which is the date that this unit was established?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My experience was that the service always had people around them to help them in their work, in their intelligence work, in everything that a secret service does. So in my experience, Frenki always had some people around him. But that this became a military unit which started to resemble an army at the company level, when this happened, I don't know. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Mr. Frenki Simatovic correct that it was founded in 1991, or is Mr. Milosevic correct that it was founded in 1995? Please just tell us which one.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that once I mentioned this when I was talking to Simatovic, and I think he said that it was some sort of internal decree authorising him to have armed men under his command. I think that was it, and I think it can be found out, and after my testimony, I'm willing to research this and to try to assist and to submit this information later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me put to you a public statement made by Mr. Milosevic around this time and see if it helps refresh your recollection as to which one of these dates is perhaps the more accurate one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I now tender an article dated the 12th of April, 1991. I'd ask that it be distributed. It's a copy of an interview with Mr. Milosevic, the 12th of April, 1991, being less than three weeks before the date that Frenki Simatovic says was the founding date of this unit. And here is a direct quote from Mr. Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let's all have this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's page 2 of the English translation that I'll be referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the date? The 12th of April?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 12th of April, 1991, and I'll read you a passage and see whether it helps you decide which is the correct date of the founding of this unit. Mr. Milosevic says: "I ordered a mobilisation of the reserve police forces yesterday. Further engagement and formation of new police forces is to follow and the government was tasked with preparing appropriate formations to guarantee our security and make us capable of defending the interest of our republic and also the interest of the Serbian people outside Serbia." Does that statement of Mr. Milosevic, indicating an order that he gave for the creation of new special forces, help you decide whether the date given by Frenki Simatovic, the 4th of May, 1991, is in fact the correct date of the founding of these forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, on the 4th of April, I arrived in Knin. On the 12th of April, I was so busy that I didn't care what the president was talking about or to read his paper or anyone's paper. So I have nothing to do with all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic, recognising that you may not have read this newspaper at the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Groome, you're re-examining.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And the extent to which you can cross-examine your own witness is limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could help us with where this interview was published, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will have a copy sent to the booth, Your Honour, and have them read the caption. I don't believe it's on the translation. I believe the booth has a copy, so if the translators could assist us and tell us the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are we giving statements or asking questions? That's really what I ask about this exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with this. Can somebody help us, please, as to the publication in which this article appears?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The English booth says that this is a weekly magazine published in Belgrade, called Nin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes. Wait a minute. One at a time. Everybody wants to speak. Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can explain. Nin, I think then and now, is the best-known weekly in Yugoslavia, both the former Yugoslavia and the present-day Serbia and Montenegro. It is the best-known weekly in the Yugoslavia of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. But I think, Mr. Groome, you've taken this as far as you can with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic, around this period of time you've told us about a number of contacts you've had with both the Krajina DB and the Serbian DB. Are you aware of any other special units that were formed during this time period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to repeat again: Can you even imagine how much work there was for an Australian, how difficult it was to come into a very primitive environment and to create, within three months, those Knindzas? I had very little time to be interested in what was going on outside our camp. There was no television, there were no media; I was completely cut off from all the events for at least three months. Only when I arrived in Belgrade in August that year I started reading newspapers. So to ask me what was going on in Belgrade at the time is completely misplaced. Or at any other place, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic, again I'd ask you, are there -- were there any units associated with the police of Serbia or the Krajina, the creation of new units, that you are aware of in the spring, summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have to tell you for the third time, I was so indifferent to all of that, with all the work, with all the obligations I had at the time. I was 27 kilos lighter at the time. The last thing I wanted to know then was who was doing what in Belgrade, or in any other place that had nothing to do with Krajina, which was the area of my responsibility. And there, I was trying to establish my own control and responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- it would be wrong for me to indulge in guesswork.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I take, then, that you've given an explanation, but you are not aware of any other units that you can tell us here today.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, one statement in this speech having to do with time, Mr. Simatovic mentions three places in Bosnia; Bratunac, Sokolac, and Rogatica and says others, and this is a quote from his speech: "In mid-spring of last year, it retreated from these parts with complete equipment, machinery, helicopters, and aircraft." Can we take it from Mr. Simatovic's statement here in May of 1997 that this would indicate that at least until the spring of 1996, Mr. Simatovic is saying these units were in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are forcing me to guess. I don't even know where Bratunac is. I wasn't interested in anything that was going on in Bosnia. I was up to my ears in all the things that I had to learn in order to survive in the chaos that was reigning then. And on top of all of that, I even had to learn the language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic, on Wednesday you testified that the first time you saw this video was after you came to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this form and shape, yes. I had seen certain things in Kula, some details, but I saw the entire film only here for the first time, and I was really impressed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been asked about portions of the speech of Mr. Simatovic prior to seeing the video, do you think you would have had an independent recollection of what he said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. As I already said, I can't tell you what went on in Kosovo and in Bosnia, but I was very well-informed about what was going in Krajina, and I stand behind everything I said about that part. Nothing could have happened there without me knowing it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned a man by the name of Dusan Orlovic, and you've told us that he was the head of the Krajina DB. Can you tell us, if you know, who was his superior? Would it have been Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, they were under the Ministry of the Interior, Milan Martic. Later, certain changes occurred wherein security was shifted to Milan Babic, and Milan Martic later moved out of Krajina, but I don't think those changes took place while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic, over the last several days, there are some of the -- some of the answers you have given would seem to create some confusion over what it is exactly you are testifying to. I want to ask you to try to clear up some of these, and to assist you, I'm going to ask that the following document be placed on the overhead projector. It's just portions of the transcript that I'd ask you to take a look at. I would like to ask you a couple of questions regarding them. So that we can eliminate the possibility that the translation has been the problem, can I ask you to testify to this portion of my examination of you in English.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Can you get a focus on this, please, or am I getting blind?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask that the directors --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it should be explained why we are shifting to the English language now. Until now, the witness has been answering in the Serbian language except for a few spontaneous remarks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... about this. If he can deal with it in English, it makes it much easier to deal with this part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic, on Wednesday --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't read this. Can I have a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't -- if you can just turn your head a bit and read from the -- that will assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask the director to zoom in on the left-hand column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Wednesday in response to a question, the question being, "Did you question Mr. Stanisic regarding who was requesting or who was forbidding you from going back to the Krajina?" you stated that it was your understanding that it was coming from the very top. It must have been either the Minister of Interior or the president, Milosevic. Do you recall making that statement on Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can the director or the usher please just slide that over a little bit to the right. A little bit more. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's an accurate account of your testimony from Wednesday, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember whether it was this way, but you remember too that I mentioned in this interview that he also said that I had entered some political waters which are not good for me, and it wasn't a good idea for me to go there again. I just mentioned that it was an opinion from the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Greater assistance --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- political summit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next day, Mr. Milosevic asked you a question: "Is it true that it was really Milan Babic who expelled from you the Krajina?" and you made the statement: "My feeling was that Milan Babic was superior to you, that he had more authority, because you had authority over him ..." and you go on. Are you now -- is it your testimony now that it was really -- you believe that Milan Babic was in fact more powerful than Mr. Milosevic and that it was him that had orchestrated Jovica Stanisic telling you that you were not to go back to the Krajina? Is that your testimony now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't see what is in dispute here. It was precisely that way, and I stand by what I'm saying. In that period, Babic had much more authority over Milosevic than the other way round, and certainly Babic had the last word. He was powerful enough to expel me, Frenki, and even Dusan Orlovic from Krajina whenever he wanted to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown an original copy of his statement. I'll be asking you a number of questions about your statement, which is now Prosecution 329.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It sounds to me as though we're going to have cross-examination on the witness's statement. This is re-examination. You can't cross-examine the witness. Hand that back, would you, Mr. Vasiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you can rehabilitate your witness, but you're not doing that. You're really cross-examining the witness. That's not the purpose of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe there are situations in which a witness has demonstrated such a sufficient departure from their original testimony that I would be permitted to put to him prior consistent statements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you asking that he be treated as hostile?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It may come to that, Your Honour, if he is reluctant to acknowledge his earlier statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, let's consider that. What's the page that you wanted to put to him, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph on page 8. I'd like to ask a few foundational questions just about the -- that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. We'll consider whether it's right that you should be able to do this. Now, I know that it's certainly a common law rule that witnesses can be treated as hostile and cross-examined on their statements. It's an unusual course, in my experience, but it is one that's followed, of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. course. Whether it's part of international practice, I don't know. We'll have to consider that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Of course we're not bound by common law rules here, and it may be right to clarify matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask you to consider one other point? Under the rules of evidence here - I'm trying to find the -- I am required to put the case to a witness. I believe to leave this witness at this stage with having said inconsistent things within his testimony and not having resolved it, I would not be able to later argue that it really was Mr. Milosevic who he's referring to, or Mr. Babic. So I believe in fairness to the witness and, in fact, in fairness to the proceedings themselves, I should be permitted to at least ask the witness what is his testimony precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So you're saying it's nothing to do with hostility but to do with clarification of what the witness has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Of apparently --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Contradictory evidence. Yes. Mr. Kay and then Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, you call witnesses at your own risk. You call witnesses to give evidence before a court, and if you don't like what they say, that is your problem if you're a party that's called that witness. You don't put a case to a witness if you're calling your own witness because there's nothing for you to put to him. You're bound by his evidence that you have called. When you're putting a case, you're cross-examining, and that's exactly the sort of thing that shouldn't happen. There shouldn't be any gain line in the Prosecution position in relation to this witness. They're just calling evidence before the Tribunal. They're not trying to win points, one would hope. They're trying to call evidence that goes to the truth of the matter. If they disagree with what a witness has said, then they must consider that. They can't start cross-examining and say, "We don't agree with your evidence." That's not the purpose of having a Prosecution calling evidence in a criminal trial, and it's a departure from that duty which can cause great problems into the positions of witnesses before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would respectfully disagree with Mr. Kay in that -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let Mr. Milosevic say something and then you can reply, Mr. Groome. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, this contradiction on which the opposite side is insisting is only fictitious and can impress only a person who is ignorant of the real relationships in Yugoslavia at the time. The opposite side, accidentally or on purpose, forgot, while asking questions, to add the words "in Krajina" rather than speaking in general terms. In fact, there is no contradiction, because it is indubitable that in Krajina, Milan Babic had the last word, not I, because I was President of Serbia, and I could influence them only politically and indirectly, which I did, among other things, through that letter where I reproached him for not accepting the Vance Plan, because I was President of Serbia. So it is indisputable that if you add the words "in Krajina," Babic was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have the point. No need -- no need to give evidence upon you. We were listening to argument. Yes Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just two points, Your Honour. I think this is different than the situation Mr. Kay is describing in that it is not the Prosecution's intent to impeach the evidence given by the witness in his examination-in-chief, it is simply to explore contradictions that have arisen after cross-examination. I'd also point out that ordinarily, in a common law system, cross-examination would be limited quite strictly to the scope of the evidence led on examination. In this particular case, Mr. Milosevic has been given great latitude and has explored new areas, including the role of Milan Babic in the removal of Mr. Vasiljkovic from the Krajina. I believe it is only proper that I now be entitled to explore this apparent contradiction with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will consider this over the adjournment. It's time for the adjournment. Mr. Groome, one matter. We have to deal with some administrative matters, so if you would tailor your re-examination to finish by 1.20 or so, in order to get the witness away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The issue arises whether the Prosecution may examine the witness upon the statement which he made concerning the witness's removal from Krajina and as to where the order came from. The first point I make is that it does not seem to the Trial Chamber that the cross-examination which secured a contradictory answer, or what may be thought to be a contradictory answer, was outside the scope of the original examination. It was to the point. But the issue which arises is whether the Prosecution should be entitled to put the statement to the witness to point out a contradiction, or a possible contradiction. The common law prevents the -- prevents such an examination and does so on the ground that a party cannot cross-examine its own witness and, as Mr. Kay points out, the party calling the witness must take the witness as it finds it and is bound by the evidence. There is an exception, as Mr. Groome has pointed out, in the case of a hostile witness, a particular procedure which involves a finding by the Court that the witness is hostile and then the party may cross-examine the witness upon his statement in order to contradict him. But we are not bound by the rules of the common law, and it does not seem appropriate to go down that particular path or try and follow that particular procedure, and indeed, Mr. Groome, in the end, has not sought to do so, and we do not think it would be right. However, we note, first of all, that the statement has been exhibited. So it is before us. Exhibit 392. So in any event, we are going to have to determine whether what is said in the statement is true or not or what conclusion we come upon -- we come to upon the examination and the cross-examination. We therefore think it right to allow the Prosecution to ask questions limited to clarifying the witness's evidence upon the point and clarifying the statement. That, we believe, would be important in the Tribunal's duty to determine the truth and to find the truth and in its overall procedures. We shall, therefore, allow the examination but limited to clarification, as we've said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljkovic, just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Has the witness got the statement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you look at your statement, Mr. Vasiljkovic, and again I'd ask you to do this part of your examination in English so there can be no chance of misinterpretation. Would it be fair to say that for the greater part of your life you've spoken the English language?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of your interaction with investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor has been in English; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the statement that you have before you -- and the statement that you have before you is not a translation of your statement but in fact the actual physical statement that you read; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that that's the actual statement that you read?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it has my initials at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any question --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between question and answer. It is impossible to continue at this pace. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any question in your mind that the document you read and initialed is the document that's before you now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look at the last paragraph on page 8, and I'd ask that a copy of that be placed on the overhead projector. Can you please read the last paragraph of page 8 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 4th of August, 1991, I was called to Belgrade by Stanisic Jovica. I actually thought I was going to receive a medal, but I was there to be relieved of my command. He told me that he was following the orders of the boss, meaning President Milosevic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you're a public figure in Serbia. Do you give interviews from time to time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give an interview to a reporter from Vreme magazine in October of 2001?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the course of that interview, did you also say that it was Mr. Milosevic who caused your removal from the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I believed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the next document that I'd ask you to take a look at, it has to do with what happened at Fruska Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to page 4 of your statement. Again, is that the original that you read and initialed when you made this statement in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to read the third paragraph that begins with the sentence, "Later..."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you tell me where to start, actually? Third -- "Later that summer..." is that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Please read that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. "Later that summer, after I left Krajina as a part of this unit was recruited by DB to train at Fruska Gora in Serbia with the Serb DB and then evolved into --" I'm sorry, I don't accept this statement. I want to -- listen, this is where it caused the problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need to wave it. Just put it down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there anything more before we go on to clarification? Is there anything more you want read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just one other portion of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you would read it, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A portion of the statement, of this statement is -- that I'm interested in asking your comment on is: "Later that summer, after I left the Krajina, a part of this unit was recruited by DB to train at Fruska Gora in Serbia with the Serb DB and then evolved into the Grey Wolves." Is that statement true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read and initial that page at the time you made your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had some discussions. I was told that this statement -- first of all, this is not my wording, this is your wording that you have taken out of a recorded conversation. This is the first time that we had a discussion, where I had a very bad memory of exact -- of exact happenings, when I didn't have a chance to investigate some of those things, and we have agreed that this statement is not going to be used because a lot of this is incorrect, it is untruthful, it has been twisted around, and it has been presented by Prosecution in their own views, not mine. And that was agreement. This is why we got all this confusion. I do not accept this statement. The statement that I accepted was the statement that we have corrected the mistakes with Mr. Sexton.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at the last page of the documents. Can I ask you to read the paragraph that appears just above your signature.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. "This statement has been read over by me in the English language and is true to the best of my knowledge and recollection as I have signed this statement voluntarily and I am aware that it might be used in the legal proceedings in the International Tribunal for the Prosecution of the persons responsible --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need to read all that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read that before you signed just underneath that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last portion of your statement that I would like to ask you about is with respect to this issue of the state security service and its control over participants that may have been in Croatia and Bosnia. Yesterday, in response to a question by Mr. Milosevic, he asked you the following and you gave the following answer: "When you say 'the service,' you mean the state security of Krajina. When you say 'the army,' you mean the army of Krajina. And when you say 'the police,' you mean the police of Krajina, and you do not imply under any of these organisations the police or State Security Service of Serbia; is that correct?"

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said, "That's right," yesterday, and you affirm that answer now.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall, a little bit later in his examination of you, he put the same question to you regarding Bosnia, and once again, you said, "Yes, precisely so." Do you want me to read the entire --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I asked you this question in connection with Krajina but I will repeat the same question linked to your knowledge regarding Bosnia. This is on page 11, second paragraph. You said that you didn't believe that a single unit or so-called paramilitary unit could have acted in Krajina without the permission of the army, the police, and the state security. Is it clear that in the case you are referring to, the army, police, and the state security of the Serbian Krajina and the Republika Srpska and not to the state security of Republic of Serbia?" And you said, "Yes, precisely so. I never referred to the police, state security, or army of Republika Srpska." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a misprint. It was Republic of Serbia. Like I said, I do not accept this statement. I'm not even sure that this is the -- there are so many things. We went over that many times. I have made another statement. I pointed out the mistakes. A lot of them were genuine mistakes. A lot of this was taken out of the context, and I honestly don't accept that this is what I have signed, and I never really -- in the way it is down now, I honestly contest this. You can accept that or not, but this is trick. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other statement that you're referring to, that's the statement that you signed last week?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender that statement so the Chamber has both statements before it in its consideration of this matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it is your statement now that the original statement before you - and I've asked that you be provided with the exact paper, not a copy - that this is a forged document? Is that what you're saying now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is absolutely misinterpreted, yes. I don't believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Now, cross-examination can be taken too far on this matter. We think you've gone far enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Vreme article which we've just spoken about, which you acknowledge, and I'm reading a quote from that article, the very precise question that we're dealing with now was put to you, and I'll put the question and the answer. The question was: "Were you linked to the state security of Krajina or Serbia?" To which you answered: "We are talking about the state security of Serbia." Do you recall being asked that question and giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a copy of the article so perhaps you can refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, it's been put to him and he's said that's not what he said. So I don't see how putting the article is going to change the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I agree. Don't put the article to him. Mr. Groome, you have got to consider where you are in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Because all it does is destroy the credibility of the witness. Now, whether you want to do that is a matter you may wish to consider. We will take both these statements, because they were made to the Tribunal. We will exhibit them. But I think you've probably taken the matter as far as you can, unless there's some separate area you want to ask the witness about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, there is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you back to the time after you've left the Krajina. You've testified that you went to Bor in Serbia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would have known or who knew that you were in Bor, Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Jovica Stanisic knew. Nikola Sainovic knew because he lives there, and some of my friends, and a detail that went in with my security guards to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than those people, did anyone else know that you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was about the most popular figure in the country, a lot more popular than Milosevic at that time, so a lot of people heard, told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Milosevic asked you whether at your invitation a unit of Arkan's Tigers came to your assistance, and you referred to a unit commanded by Legija coming to your assistance. At that time, was Legija a member of Arkan's unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's in 1993 in Krajina. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the same Legija that we've seen in the video that was played here on Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where is Korenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Korenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Korenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Korenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Korenica, yes. That's to the north of Knin, north-west of Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can the usher be relieved?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall testifying here in the last couple of days that Major Filipovic -- well, what DB, what state security service was he a member of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbian DB.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall in your statement, page 8, where you say -- I'll just read the following so you can recall it: "Major Filipovic, Fico, of the DB, I don't know if he was from the Belgrade or Krajina --" at the time you made the statement -- "was in charge of the Korenica region at that time."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "in charge," I meant that he was gathering information from that region. This is what we -- you know, like Frenki was in charge of the Knin area and Fico was in charge of the, you know -- I think that was just in the speech, where they were operating and getting the information on the situation, what it was there. That was in the open, in our discussion. But I think you have put it there in your own words as "in charge." I think there is a tape recording of that. I think there should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified Wednesday that you received threats from the DB after you went against Seselj to try to resolve a student protest at the law faculty.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it occur to you as odd -- well, at the time did you believe that you were the subject of legitimate, reliable death threats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it occur to you as odd that the DB appeared willing to kill you over a confrontation with Seselj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did appear to me that they wanted me out of the country, and threats with the kill wasn't just a threat that if I don't go I might end up that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown page 10 of his statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you were interviewed and you discussed this particular event, and I'll draw your attention, if you would, to the first paragraph, to the sentence beginning with, "They..." and I'll read it to you. "They basically told me that the time had come for me to go away from the Balkans. It was suggested to me that my life was in danger and that they wanted to know how much it would cost for me to disappear. They told me that this order had come from the top. By this I knew that they were talking about President Milosevic." Do you stand behind those words today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to some extent. I believe that that was coming from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that point in time, you believe that Mr. Milosevic had given an order to the security DB to get you out of the country, and if you did not go, to have you killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I constructed in my mind, yeah, with my knowledge that I had at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milosevic has asked you a number of questions about protections you may or may not have sought. I just want to ask you a few more. Before you came to testify here, did you notify an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor of two events which caused you concern; one a journalist had somehow learned that you were going to testify, and second, a text message that you received on your phone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but that was not specifically -- I did not contact or notify them specifically, but that was part of the context of the other communications I had with the investigator. Yes, I did inform him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what the text message was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that I have received a message which mentions Legija, but I don't honestly don't -- I don't believe that it has anything to do with him. I have made inquiries, and I found out -- and I told him that has nothing to do with him, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said you made inquiries, you actually checked out the number from where this came.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used some connections and friends that I had in the secret service, in the police, even in the army, and we tracked down where these numbers come from and who were the people that made it, and we did not connect it to Legija, Milosevic, or the Tribunal, and I have informed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many numbers were registered to the exact same person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifty-eight numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that make you believe that that was not the phone of a private individual but of somebody in some secret service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no secret service. I thought it was the part of an organisation. I thought it was some sort of a political -- I suspected Seselj, actually, at the time, but it turned out to be something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few other matters on your security. You said that you did not begin cooperating with the Office the Prosecutor until after the law on cooperation. You said that earlier today. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think -- I felt -- I don't know. I don't know. I think we had some meetings, but I think that I come -- that I come to -- that we sat down and done some -- start doing some work after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you the Gazette where the law on cooperation was passed, simply for the purpose of helping you remember the date that the law on cooperation was passed. Can you tell us the date of the Gazette.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: April 2002.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the date of the statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VASILJKOVIC [Resumed]
